subject: Concord integration: SDK compatibility checklist & deprecation impact
messages:
From: Elena Korzun <elena@concordtech.com>
To: rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
Cc: diego.ramos@concordtech.com
Date: Wed, 14 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Heads-up: Concord SDK v1 deprecation and compatibility ask

Hi Rafael —

Quick context: Concord is planning to deprecate the public SDK v1 surface on 2027-01-15. We run a number of customers who use Redwood’s connector for live model routing; after an internal audit we found a few integration points in our connector that rely on endpoints that will be removed in v2.

Before we publish the public deprecation notice next week, we wanted to reach out to Redwood to:

- Confirm whether Redwood’s partner connector will continue to function against Concord v2 or if we should expect any breaking calls.
- Ask for a compatibility checklist (endpoints, versions, any breaking semantic changes).
- Propose a short joint testing window + a compatibility scoreboard so both teams can sign off.

I attached our internal deprecation notice (concord-deprec-notice.pdf) and a very short list of the endpoints we think are impacted.

Can you loop in product/engineering so we can map out a migration path? We’d like to avoid forcing our mutual customers to perform emergency migrations.

Thanks,
Elena
Partnerships — Concord Tech
attachments: concord-deprec-notice.pdf
From: rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
To: Elena Korzun <elena@concordtech.com>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 14 Oct 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Heads-up: Concord SDK v1 deprecation and compatibility ask

Elena —

Thanks for the heads-up and for sharing the notice. I’ve looped in Vanessa (Product) and Marissa (Integrations) so we can do a quick triage. Initial thoughts:

- We need a simple compatibility matrix that maps Concord endpoints -> Redwood connector surface area.
- For any breaking change, we can offer a short-term shim adapter on Redwood Dedicated to keep traffic stable while customers migrate; we’ll need to understand performance/latency impact.
- We should jointly define a test harness (smoke tests + at least one end-to-end customer run) during your proposed window.

I attached a quick starter workbook (redwood-initial-compat-notes.xlsx) — it contains the endpoints you sent plus two rows we flagged as high-risk.

Proposed next steps:
1) Vanessa to propose a compatibility scoreboard and mitigation options by EOD Thu (10/15).
2) Schedule a 45-min sync next week (slots below).
3) Agree on mutual action plan and public comms schedule before you publish the notice.

Available times for the sync: Thu 10/15 09:00–11:00 PT or Fri 10/16 13:00–16:00 PT. Which works best for your engineering lead?

—Rafael
Senior Partner Manager, Redwood Inference
redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123
attachments: redwood-initial-compat-notes.xlsx
From: Diego Ramos <diego.ramos@concordtech.com>
To: rafael_mendes@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: Elena Korzun <elena@concordtech.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Oct 2026 07:41:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Heads-up: Concord SDK v1 deprecation and compatibility ask

Rafael + Vanessa —

Thanks for the quick reply. A few clarifications from engineering:

- Timeline is firm: v1 will enter read-only mode 2026-12-15, full cutover 2027-01-15. We can push an extended grace window for partners if there’s a coordinated plan.
- Key breaking changes: auth header semantics (we move to signed tokens instead of bearer headers), batch-insert endpoint removed (we will replace with a streaming append API), and a slight schema tightening for the /metadata payload (older optional fields become required).
- We depend on Redwood’s connector for two flows: live routing (low latency) and async ingestion (batch). The live flow is the higher risk.

We’d prefer a joint test harness run w/ a Redwood test account and one small customer (non-production) during the week of 2026-12-06.

Happy to take the 10/16 14:00 PT slot if that works.

—Diego
Staff Engineer, Concord Tech
From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
To: Elena Korzun <elena@concordtech.com>, diego.ramos@concordtech.com
Cc: rafael_mendes@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 16 Oct 2026 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Heads-up: Concord SDK v1 deprecation and compatibility ask

Diego / Elena —

Appreciate the details — that timeline is tight but workable with a few guardrails. Summary of Redwood’s proposed approach:

1) Compatibility scoreboard (attached: compatibility-scoreboard.csv) — a three-column map: endpoint | risk (low/medium/high) | mitigation. High-risk items: auth header change (high), batch->stream API (high), metadata schema tightening (medium).

2) Mitigation options (short list):
   - Adapter shim: short-lived adapter that translates Concord v2 -> v1 semantics for the live routing path (we can host on Dedicated pools for affected customers). Expected: 2–3 weeks of engineering + validation.
   - Customer-side SDK patch: we can co-release a small SDK helper with Concord that does header translation and schema compatibility checks. Lower latency but requires action by customers.
   - Joint test harness: Redwood will provide a dev cluster + a synthetic traffic runner. We ask Concord to provide a dev credentials bundle and the list of test payloads.

3) Proposed schedule:
   - 10/19: Redwood delivers full compatibility scoreboard and rough effort estimates (engineering points + perf notes).
   - 11/01: Mutual agreement on mitigation option(s) and which customers to include in a pilot.
   - 12/06 week: Joint test harness (non-prod) run.

4) SLAs/comms: If we opt for the Adapter shim path, Redwood asks Concord to add a Partner Exception to the public deprecation notice (2-week extended grace window) so we can coordinate cutover with customers.

Inline responses to Diego’s bullets:
> On Thu, Oct 15, 2026 at 07:41 AM, Diego Ramos <diego.ramos@concordtech.com> wrote:
>
> - Timeline is firm: v1 will enter read-only mode 2026-12-15, full cutover 2027-01-15.

We can work to those dates if we lock scope by 11/01.

> - Key breaking changes: auth header semantics ... batch-insert endpoint removed ... schema tightening.

We will prioritize auth and batch->stream in the scoreboard; metadata tightening is likely a per-customer validation task.

Next steps: Rafael — can you confirm the 10/19 scoreboard delivery in your calendar and lock the 12/06 test window on the Concord side? Elena — can Concord share dev creds and the small test-customer candidate by 10/22?

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Principal Product Manager, Redwood Inference
redwood.ai

All —

Thanks everyone for the fast sync. Confirming next steps and owners (mutual action plan draft attached):

- 10/22 (Concord): Dev creds + small non-prod customer candidate. Owner: Elena (concord).
- 11/01 (Joint): Decision on mitigation path (Adapter shim OR co-released SDK helper) and list of pilot customers. Owner: rafael_mendes@redwood.ai + Elena.
- 12/06 week: Joint non-prod test harness run. Owner: integrations + Concord eng.
- 12/15: Concord v1 read-only date (targets in public comms to be finalized).

I’ll block the 10/19 calendar item now and schedule the 45-min decision sync for 11/01 09:00 PT. Elena — can you confirm the 10/16 14:00 PT slot is OK for a quick engineer-to-engineer call?
